headline: DFA Rebukes Chinese Envoy Over Remark on Winning by Force
seoTitle: DFA rebukes Chinese envoy over force remark
seoDescription: The DFA urged restraint after Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan said Beijing could easily win if it used force, while saying China would not do so.
deck: Manila called the envoy's words unhelpful to already complicated ties; his complete statement also rejected using force and said China wanted peace.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What was said
paragraphs: The Department of Foreign Affairs urged Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan to exercise greater restraint after remarks that the agency said appeared to convey a thinly veiled threat of force.
Jing said China could easily win if it chose to use force, but added in the same statement that China would not do so and wanted peace.

sections.heading: The Philippine response
paragraphs: The DFA said diplomacy requires tact and restraint so that dialogue can continue despite differences. It called the wording regrettable and unhelpful amid complicated bilateral ties.
The agency asked diplomats accredited to the Philippines to avoid language that could erode trust or derail constructive engagement.

sections.heading: China's response and unresolved points
paragraphs: The Chinese Embassy said the remarks had been selectively quoted and overinterpreted. Beijing said the relationship was at an extremely sensitive stage.
The reports do not establish an imminent plan to use force. The next concrete signals are any formal diplomatic action and the state of bilateral maritime communication channels.

sections.heading: Why it matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Statements by senior diplomats can affect crisis management around Philippine vessels and communities in the West Philippine Sea.
Clear attribution matters: the DFA's criticism is confirmed, while broader claims about either government's intentions require separate evidence.
